title: Compose blog module
description: Maintaining the blog-compose core module, Compose Blog Engine, and admin compose editor.

blocks.text: blog-compose is a cross-vertical core module under packages/core/modules/blog-compose/. It implements the first blog engine variant: Compose (declarative JSON blocks). The module is registered in packages/core/modules.json with prismaFragment prisma/blog-compose.prisma and feature flag blogCompose.

blocks.code:
BlogPost (Prisma)
  contentJson: ComposeDocument
       ↓
ComposeBlogRenderer (interpreter)
       ↓
Block components (Tailwind)

Admin: COMPOSE_BLOCK_REGISTRY → field defs → BlogComposePanel
       ↓
/api/blog-posts → BlogComposeService

rows: Admin tab — meta form, block list, preview

blocks.text: Blog sidebar is not enabled by default. Install with blog-compose+sidebar (or pnpm template:add-module bakery blog-compose+sidebar) to set SITE.features.blogSidebar. parseModuleSpecs in module-installer-core.mjs splits +extras; moduleInstallOptionsFromSpecs enables the flag.

blocks.title: Dev Agency walkthrough
blocks.text: Developers → Templates → Dev Agency Website documents blog-compose+sidebar as the optional add-on example for a lean agency landing (expertise, team, work carousel) plus a later technical blog.

blocks.code:
pnpm template:add-module scaffold blog-compose+sidebar
# Docsite demo: /blog has sidebar always; /blog/playground for JSON experiments

items: Extend the block union and ComposeBlockType in lib/blog/compose/types.ts
Add a ComposeBlockDefinition entry in registry.ts (fields for admin UI)
Implement the React component in blocks/text-blocks.tsx or blocks/media-blocks.tsx
Export types from lib/blog/compose/index.ts if needed

blocks.text: Annotation features (highlight, underline, future marks) use string arrays on explain blocks. AnnotatedText splits text by phrase matches — phrases must appear exactly in the body text.

items: applyAdminTabRegistry merges Blog articles tab (BookOpen icon) into app/admin/registry.ts
applyModulesHomePage adds BlogSection to scaffold app/page.tsx

blocks.text: BlogPost.engine defaults to compose. A future editor-based engine would use a different engine id, content shape, and interpreter. Keep compose isolated under lib/blog/compose/ so new engines can live alongside (e.g. lib/blog/editor/).
